title: High Molecular Weight Genomic DNA Extraction from Coral Sperm
author: David Hayward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.nwhdfb6
materials: lysis buffer (10mM Tris pH 8; 100mM EDTA; 0.5% SDS)

9. Transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh 50ml falcon tube. The aqueous phase can be very viscous and difficult to handle- sacrifice yield for purity. If needed MaxTract High density (Qiagen) can be used to aid phase separation – this may require addition of extra chloroform.

steps.title: Grind frozen sperm powder
steps.instruction: Grind frozen sperm to a fine powder in liquid nitrogen using a pre‑cooled mortar and pestle.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer and mix
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of lysis buffer (10 mM Tris pH 8, 100 mM EDTA, 0.5 % SDS) per gram of starting material to the frozen powder and mix; the mixture will freeze quickly because of the sub‑zero temperature of the mortar.

steps.title: Thaw mixture with gentle mixing
steps.instruction: Allow the mixture to thaw while gently mixing with the pestle to ensure even dispersion of the tissue throughout the lysis buffer.

steps.title: Transfer to tube and add RNase A
steps.instruction: Place the thawed mixture in a 50 mL Falcon tube and add RNase A (DNase‑free) to a final concentration of 20 µg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Incubate with RNase A
steps.instruction: Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour with periodic gentle mixing.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and incubate
steps.instruction: Add Proteinase K to a final concentration of 100 µg mL⁻¹ and incubate at 50 °C for 3 hours with periodic gentle mixing.

steps.title: Phenol/chloroform/isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) and gently rotate end‑over‑end for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge extraction mixture
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 5 000 g for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Repeat phenol/chloroform extractions
steps.instruction: Repeat the phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol extraction twice, then perform a final phenol/chloroform extraction (without isoamyl alcohol).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with acetate and isopropanol
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA by adding 1/9 volume 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 0.6 volume isopropanol; mix gently until the DNA comes out of solution.

steps.title: Ethanol washes of DNA precipitate
steps.instruction: If the yield is sufficient, collect the DNA with a sealed glass Pasteur pipette or a Gilson tip and transfer it to a large volume of 70 % ethanol; mix gently for 5 minutes at room temperature, then repeat the 70 % ethanol wash at least two times (by transferring to fresh ethanol or by replacing the ethanol).

substeps.instruction: Collect DNA with Pasteur pipette or Gilson tip.
Mix DNA in large volume of 70 % ethanol for 5 min at RT.
Repeat ethanol wash ≥2 times, using fresh 70 % ethanol each time.

steps.title: Collect and air‑dry DNA
steps.instruction: Collect the DNA using a sealed glass Pasteur pipette or Gilson tip and allow it to air‑dry.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Place the dried DNA in an appropriate volume of 1X TE (or 0.1X TE if EDTA is problematic) to allow it to detach from the pipette tip; expect a yield >1 mg per gram of starting material and store at 4 °C. Dissolution may take hours to days.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation if needed
steps.instruction: If the yield is not high enough to remove the DNA with a pipette, centrifuge to pellet the DNA and wash the pellet at least two times with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dialyze for high‑molecular‑weight DNA
steps.instruction: For very high molecular weight DNA, dialyze the aqueous phase from the final phenol/chloroform extraction extensively against 50 mM Tris (pH 8) and 10 mM EDTA (or 0.1X TE if EDTA is problematic) until the OD260/280 exceeds 1.8, changing the dialysis buffer several times over at least two days.
